root_idea.summary: The root denotes forceful joining and interlocking of one thing with another, producing compactness and the absence of intervening gaps.
root_idea.development: From strong joining, the semantic field extends to firmly compact structures, close ranks, fixed placement, and other close-fitting applications. Lead is associated with the root in the lexicographic tradition because of the compactness attributed to its particles.

qac_form_accounting.reason: The Quran-attested passive participle is presented under its normalized Classical Arabic citation form.

senses.definition: Firmly joined and made compact, with its parts tightly integrated and leaving no intervening gaps.
senses.usage_conditions: In the Quranic occurrence, the adjectival passive participle describes a structure whose component parts are solidly joined; the comparison is to something constructed as though with lead.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To close or lock a door; also to seal an opening, such as the mouth of a vessel, firmly.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The vessel-mouth wording is reported with a possible textual reading issue; the lexical use is retained as a sealing or stopping-up construction.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To arrange eggs evenly or level.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Said of a domestic hen or an ostrich arranging its eggs with its bill and feet.

other_classical_meanings.definition: For a woman, to put on a face veil so that only the eyes are visible.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A specialized face-veiling construction, noted as a dialectal usage of Temeem.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To veil oneself with the face covering called niqāb.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Described as a less emphatic form of the close veiling expressed by تَرْصِيص; the evidence does not independently specify the precise amount of facial coverage.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To be importunate or urgent in asking or begging.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A figurative or specialized usage marked as tropical in the lexical evidence.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To place oneself close together in a rank or ranks, leaving no intervening space.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Used especially of people standing in ranks for prayer or battle.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To continue or become fixed or settled in a place.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Attested in the construction رَصْرَصَ فِي الْمَكَانِ.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Closeness or nearness together of the teeth.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A nominal description of teeth that are close together.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Lead, the mineral; also a piece of lead.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The lexical evidence records several vocalic variants of the noun.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A stone, or stones fitted closely around a running spring; stones heaped together on a grave.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The plural رَصَائِصُ is used for stones heaped upon a grave.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A niggard or miser.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A figurative use likening the person to a stone.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A manufacturer or seller of lead.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A reported occupational noun referring either to a lead manufacturer or a lead seller.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Hard ground or hard land.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: An independently reported nominal usage.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Having teeth that are close together.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The masculine adjective is explicitly applied to a man; its feminine counterpart is رَصَّاءُ.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Describing a woman as sexually impervious or inaccessible to intercourse.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A specialized feminine adjectival usage.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Having thighs close together, with one thigh cleaving or sticking to the other.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Used of a woman or of a thigh in the lexical descriptions.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A cap or head covering shaped like a melon.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A specialized noun for a particular kind of qalansuwa.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Set one upon another or arranged compactly, as eggs.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A classical application distinct from the Quranic description of a firmly integrated structure.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Overlaid or lined with lead.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Applied, for example, to a well cased with lead; this is a literal lead-covering sense distinct from compact joining.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A face veil drawn near a woman’s eyes.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A specialized noun for a niqāb positioned close to the eyes.

lane_unit_coverage.note: Joining and firming a structure is covered by the Quranic sense; closing or sealing openings is separately represented.
Close formation in prayer or battle represented.
Stones set closely together are covered by the broader compact-joining sense.
Fixed or settled in a place represented.
Lead mineral and piece-of-lead noun represented.
Face veil drawn near the eyes represented.
Stone and closely fitted-stones usage represented.
A thigh cleaving to its fellow is covered by the close-thighed meaning.
Firmly compact building sense and compactly set eggs are both represented.

cautions: The Quranic form is attested only as the adjectival passive participle مَرْصُوصٌ in 61:4; the lead-related and specialized derived meanings belong to broader Classical Arabic usage unless independently tied to the Quranic construction.
The report concerning the mouth of a vessel includes a possible textual reading issue; it is retained as a qualified sealing use rather than treated as fully certain.
